claims.text: The illustrative baseline refractory HEA is predominantly single-phase BCC and contains Nb, Mo, Ta, W, and minor Al.
Controlled oxidation during powder-metallurgy synthesis can produce an in situ Y2O3 dispersion in the refractory HEA.
The oxide dispersion will occupy less than 3 vol% of the modified alloy.
The intervention will produce a fine, homogeneous distribution of Y2O3 nanoparticles both within grains and at grain boundaries.
Y2O3 nanoparticles within the grains will pin or impede dislocations.
Y2O3 nanoparticles at grain boundaries will retard grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperature.
Impeded dislocation motion will enhance high-temperature yield strength.
Retarded grain-boundary sliding will enhance high-temperature creep resistance.
A low, well-dispersed nanoparticle volume fraction will minimally disturb room-temperature dislocation mechanisms.
The oxide-dispersed alloy will preserve room-temperature yield strength relative to the oxide-free baseline.
The oxide-dispersed alloy will preserve room-temperature ductility relative to the oxide-free baseline.
The oxide-dispersed alloy will improve high-temperature yield strength or creep resistance by approximately 20–30% relative to the oxide-free baseline at 800–1200°C.
Adding less than 3 vol% of lightweight oxide nanoparticles will not appreciably increase alloy density.
The predicted benefit is limited to processing and service conditions under which the nanoscale oxide dispersion remains stable and does not coarsen or destabilize during thermal cycling.
